ECC.P.3.1-8.text: To Everything There Is a Season

ECC.P.9.1-6.text: Death Comes to Good and Bad

ECC.P.9.7-12.text: Enjoy Your Portion in This Life

ECC.P.11.1-6.text: Cast Your Bread upon the Waters

ECC.1.1-3.text: The Teacher says everything is futile and asks what work gains

ECC.1.4-6.text: The Teacher says generations pass, but the earth, sun and wind repeat

ECC.1.7-8.text: The Teacher says rivers and all things are wearisome and never satisfy

ECC.1.9-11.text: The Teacher says nothing is new and people are forgotten

ECC.1.12-15.text: The Teacher, king in Jerusalem, finds all human work futile

ECC.1.16-18.text: The Teacher learns that much wisdom brings much sorrow

ECC.2.1-2.text: The Teacher tests pleasure and finds it futile

ECC.2.3-3.text: The Teacher tries wine and folly to see what is worthwhile

ECC.2.4-6.text: The Teacher builds houses, vineyards, gardens and reservoirs

ECC.2.7-8.text: The Teacher gathers servants, flocks, silver, gold and singers

ECC.2.9-10.text: The Teacher becomes great and denies himself no pleasure

ECC.2.11-11.text: The Teacher sees that all his work gains nothing

ECC.2.12-12.text: The Teacher turns to think about wisdom and folly

ECC.2.13-14.text: The Teacher sees wisdom is better than folly, but both share one fate

ECC.2.15-16.text: The Teacher sees that the wise and the fool will both die and be forgotten

ECC.2.17-17.text: The Teacher hates life because all work is futile

ECC.2.18-18.text: The Teacher hates his work because he must leave it to another

ECC.2.19-20.text: The Teacher despairs because an unknown man will take his work

ECC.2.21-23.text: The Teacher says leaving work to one who did not earn it is futile

ECC.2.24-25.text: The Teacher says enjoying food and work is from God

ECC.2.26-26.text: The Teacher says God gives joy to the pleasing but not the sinner

ECC.3.1-3.text: The Teacher says there is a time for every purpose, such as birth and death

ECC.3.4-5.text: The Teacher lists times to weep, laugh, mourn and dance

ECC.3.6-7.text: The Teacher lists times to search, keep, tear, mend, be silent and speak

ECC.3.8-8.text: The Teacher says there is a time to love, to hate, for war and for peace

ECC.3.9-10.text: The Teacher asks what work gains and notes the burden God gave people

ECC.3.11-11.text: The Teacher says God made all things beautiful, but people cannot understand his work

ECC.3.12-13.text: The Teacher says people should rejoice, do good and enjoy their work as God’s gift

ECC.3.14-15.text: The Teacher says God’s work lasts forever so that people will fear him

ECC.3.16-17.text: The Teacher sees wickedness in courts, but says God will judge everyone

ECC.3.18-18.text: God tests people to show them they are like animals

ECC.3.19-20.text: Men and animals share the same breath and the same end

ECC.3.21-22.text: No one knows what comes after death, so enjoy your work

ECC.4.1-1.text: The Preacher sees the tears of the oppressed

ECC.4.2-3.text: The Preacher thinks the dead and the unborn are better off

ECC.4.4-4.text: Work and success come from envy of a neighbor

ECC.4.5-6.text: A fool does nothing; a quiet handful is better than toil

ECC.4.7-8.text: A man alone works without end and has no one to enjoy it

ECC.4.9-11.text: Two people are better than one because they help each other

ECC.4.12-12.text: Two can resist an attacker, and a cord of three is strong

ECC.4.13-14.text: A poor wise youth is better than a foolish old king

ECC.4.15-16.text: People follow the new king, but later people forget him

ECC.5.1-1.text: Be careful and listen when you go to God’s house

ECC.5.2-3.text: The Preacher tells worshipers to speak few words to God

ECC.5.4-5.text: Worshipers must keep their vows to God quickly

ECC.5.6-7.text: Worshipers must not excuse a broken vow, but fear God

ECC.5.8-9.text: Do not be surprised at oppression; officials watch officials

ECC.5.10-11.text: Those who love money are never satisfied with it

ECC.5.12-12.text: A worker sleeps well, but the rich man cannot sleep

ECC.5.13-14.text: Wealth can be lost, leaving nothing for a man’s son

ECC.5.15-17.text: A man leaves with nothing and lives in sorrow and anger

ECC.5.18-18.text: It is good to enjoy work and food in the days God gives

ECC.5.19-20.text: God gives wealth and joy as a gift to people

ECC.6.1-2.text: God gives a man riches, but a stranger enjoys them

ECC.6.3-4.text: A man with many children but no joy is worse than a stillborn child

ECC.6.5-6.text: The stillborn child has more rest than a man without joy

ECC.6.7-8.text: People work to eat, yet are never satisfied

ECC.6.9-12.text: No one knows what is good for people in their short lives

ECC.7.1-2.text: A good name and a house of mourning teach people well

ECC.7.3-4.text: Sorrow is better than laughter; the wise think of death

ECC.7.5-6.text: A wise person’s rebuke is better than fools’ songs

ECC.7.7-7.text: Extortion and bribes harm even a wise man

ECC.7.8-9.text: Patience is better than pride; anger belongs to fools

ECC.7.10-10.text: The Teacher warns against longing for the old days

ECC.7.11-12.text: Wisdom is good and protects the life of its owner

ECC.7.13-13.text: No one can straighten what God has bent

ECC.7.14-14.text: Be joyful in good times; God also sends hard times

ECC.7.15-16.text: The Teacher warns against being too righteous or too wise

ECC.7.17-18.text: Whoever fears God avoids wickedness and folly

ECC.7.19-20.text: Wisdom is strong, but no one is always righteous

ECC.7.21-22.text: The Teacher says not to listen to every word spoken

ECC.7.23-25.text: The Teacher tests wisdom but cannot fully understand

ECC.7.26-26.text: The Teacher warns of a woman who is like a snare

ECC.7.27-28.text: The Teacher finds few upright people among many

ECC.7.29-29.text: God made people upright, but people seek many schemes

ECC.8.2-4.text: The Teacher says to obey the king’s command

ECC.8.5-7.text: A wise heart knows the right time to act

ECC.8.8-9.text: No one has power over the day of death

ECC.8.10-11.text: Slow punishment leads people to do more evil

ECC.8.12-13.text: It will go well for people who fear God

ECC.8.14-15.text: Life is unfair, so the Teacher commends enjoying life

ECC.8.16-17.text: No one can fully understand God’s work

ECC.9.1-1.text: The righteous and wise are in God’s hands

ECC.9.2-2.text: The same fate comes to the righteous and the wicked

ECC.9.3-3.text: All people face one fate, and all join the dead

ECC.9.4-5.text: The living have hope, but the dead know nothing

ECC.9.6-6.text: The dead no longer share in life under the sun

ECC.9.7-8.text: People should eat and drink with joy

ECC.9.9-10.text: People should enjoy life with a wife and work hard

ECC.9.11-12.text: Time and chance come to all, and bad times come suddenly

ECC.9.13-15.text: A poor wise man saves a small city but is forgotten

ECC.9.16-16.text: People despise a poor man’s wisdom and ignore his words

ECC.9.17-18.text: Wise calm words are heeded; one sinner destroys much good

ECC.10.1-3.text: A little folly spoils wisdom, and a fool shows his folly

ECC.10.4-4.text: A calm person stays at his post when a ruler is angry

ECC.10.5-7.text: The Teacher sees fools in high places and slaves on horses

ECC.10.8-9.text: Workers can be hurt by digging, quarrying or splitting logs

ECC.10.10-11.text: Skill brings success, as a dull axe needs more strength

ECC.10.12-12.text: A wise man’s words are kind, but a fool’s words ruin him

ECC.10.13-14.text: A fool’s many words begin in folly and end in evil madness

ECC.10.15-15.text: A fool grows tired and does not know the way to the city

ECC.10.16-17.text: A land with a noble king and wise princes is blessed

ECC.10.18-19.text: Laziness ruins a house, and money is the answer to all

ECC.10.20-20.text: People should not curse the king or the rich, even in secret

ECC.11.1-3.text: People should give freely, since no one knows what comes

ECC.11.4-5.text: Whoever watches the wind and clouds fails to sow or reap

ECC.11.6-6.text: People should sow morning and evening; success is unknown

ECC.11.7-8.text: People should rejoice in life, but remember the dark days

ECC.11.9-10.text: A young man should rejoice, but God will judge his actions

ECC.12.1-2.text: The Teacher warns of hard years when pleasure is gone

ECC.12.3-3.text: Strong men stoop and those who watch see dimly

ECC.12.4-4.text: Doors shut, the mill is quiet, and sounds grow faint

ECC.12.5-5.text: Man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets

ECC.12.6-7.text: Before death, the dust returns to earth and spirit to God

ECC.12.8-8.text: The Teacher says that everything is futile

ECC.12.9-9.text: The Teacher was wise and taught the people knowledge

ECC.12.10-11.text: The Teacher wrote true words; wise words are like goads

ECC.12.12-12.text: The Teacher warns his son that much study is tiring

ECC.12.13-14.text: People must fear God, for he will judge every deed
